target_customer: Organizations that process large volumes of paper and PDF documents by hand
problem: Paperwork has to be keyed into systems manually. Docucharm used NLP and AI to turn documents into structured data.

exit.reason: Not public. A vendor directory says operations ceased in 2020.

technical_complexity.rationale: Extracting structured fields from varied documents with NLP was standard but hard to generalize in 2019 for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of proprietary data, integrations or customers. Document extraction was a crowded, copyable category.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced incumbent action against Docucharm. The company stopped operating by about 2020.

market_need_then: Manual document handling was a known enterprise cost, but no Docucharm specific evidence of demand was found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material found about the name or identity.

outcome_analysis: Docucharm was a two person Winter 2019 company listed as inactive by YC, with a vendor directory dating the end of operations to 2020. No post-mortem, press coverage or funding announcement was found, so the cause of failure is not public and no failure factor is asserted.
notes: Funding of about $150K from YC and Liquid 2 Ventures appears only on CB Insights (unverified, not recorded as a round). Stanford TechIndex lists it Active, judged stale. No website listed in the directory. Founding year not found. Competitor search returned only undated listicles about later firms, so the list is empty. The recorded seed (150K, March 2019) rests on a single database (CB Insights). Stanford TechIndex shows no funding total.
